summary: Defines managed objects for source routing and source routing transparent bridges, which join Token Ring segments. These bridges are also expected to implement the relevant groups of the Bridge MIB. It is now historic.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines management data for source-routing bridges, which connect network segments and use routing information carried by frames. It lists settings and counters that a network manager can inspect or change through the network-management framework.

subtitle: SNMP objects for monitoring and configuring source-routing bridges.

tldr.problem: Network managers need a defined set of measurements and settings for source-routing bridges.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds a Management Information Base group with per-port settings and counters, plus an optional port-pair group.
tldr.outcome: The memo is Historic and supersedes the source-routing objects in RFC 1286.

today: RFC 1525 is Historic. It superseded the source-routing MIB group in RFC 1286.

sections.title: Managing Source-Routing Bridges
sections.content:
A bridge connects local network segments. A source-routing bridge uses route information in a frame to guide forwarding, and a source-routing transparent bridge combines this behavior with transparent bridging.

This RFC defines Management Information Base (MIB) objects for managing those bridges. It extends the Bridge MIB and expects a device implementing these objects to implement the relevant Bridge MIB groups as well.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC describes information that management software can read or set on a source-routing bridge. It adds to the existing management objects for bridges.

sections.title: Per-Port Settings and Counters
sections.content:
The dot1dSr group describes source-routing state. Its per-port table includes values such as the local and target segment, bridge number, maximum frame size, and spanning-tree-explorer behavior.

The table also counts received and transmitted source-routed, all-paths-explorer, and spanning-tree-explorer frames. Other counters record frames discarded for invalid or duplicate segment information, excessive route length, and related errors.
sections.plainLanguage: Each bridge port has settings that describe its segments and forwarding behavior. Counters show how many frames arrived, left, or were discarded for specific reasons.

sections.title: Optional Port-Pair Information
sections.content:
The dot1dPortPair group is optional. A bridge uses it when it supports the port-pair multiport model described by the referenced IEEE addendum.

Each entry identifies a pair of bridge ports, the bridge number for the path between them, and the state of that entry. Setting the state to invalid(3) removes the corresponding entry.
sections.plainLanguage: Some bridges can expose information about paths that connect pairs of ports. This part of the MIB is optional and lets a manager enable, disable, or remove a path entry.

sections.title: Relationship to Other Management Data
sections.content:
The source-routing MIB avoids objects that duplicate information in the Bridge MIB, the system group, or the interfaces group. Port identifiers refer to bridge ports and do not have to match interface identifiers.

The RFC supersedes the source-routing group from RFC 1286 and records changes made to align the definitions with updates to the source-routing bridge addendum. Its security section says security issues are not discussed.
sections.plainLanguage: The new objects complement the general bridge and interface information instead of repeating it. This Historic RFC superseded the earlier definitions in RFC 1286.
